conceptZh: 陽：太陽的光，左邊是土丘（阜），右邊是太陽升起的樣子。
object: a boxy mismatched-parts toy robot with one very long arm, a big glossy toy sun with rosy cheeks
morph: two teams tug a rope: robot pulls the sun's side, the sun pulls the hill side, and the two halves of 陽 spring together
creativeAngle: 玩具機器人與玩具太陽拔河，一拉一扯讓左右兩半彈在一起；長短手機器人用長手臂把太陽拉上來。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean 2D/3D toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 陽 (sun / sunshine), correctly formed, in a saturated solid color against a much lighter background, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with margins. Lead cast: a boxy mismatched-parts toy robot with one very long arm, a big glossy toy sun with rosy cheeks. Soft sky-blue backdrop with a small sandy-yellow hill mound at the bottom; the glyph is built in deep sunset-orange. Timed beats. 0.0-1.5s: the boxy toy robot (mismatched copper and teal parts, long left arm) marches in dragging a thick rope that runs off the right edge. As it plants its feet, the voice says the first 陽 and a faint orange outline of the left half (the hill radical) appears at center, bobbing. 1.5-3.0s: the rope tightens and a rosy-cheeked toy sun slides up from the right edge, gripping the other end with both rays. They tug-of-war; the robot's long arm stretches comically while the sun squeaks backwards. The voice says the second 陽 as the two orange halves of the glyph stretch apart like taffy. 3.0-4.5s: the rope snaps slack, robot and sun both shoot back, and the two halves spring together with a boing into the finished solid orange 陽 at about 70% of frame height. The robot tumbles onto its back with its legs spinning. 4.5-5.0s: the voice says 太陽 (ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ) as the real toy sun hops up beside the glyph and beams warm rays across the robot, who flips upright and salutes with the long arm. Final hold: 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still. The sun gently sways and the robot waves its mismatched arms off to the side, never touching the strokes. The glyph holds fully still and clearly readable for the last 3 seconds. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 陽、陽、太陽 (ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, and stop; no other speech, subtitles or loud music. The vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 陽 is the only text on screen: no subtitles, captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, flashing or strobing effects, and no real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon animals.

conceptZh: 大怪獸想抱走山丘上的玩具太陽，發條鯊魚卻咬住太陽垂下的長光帶，兩個拉來拉去、腳底打滑，光帶「啵」地鬆開，兩個都跌坐在地，怪獸把山丘撞成左邊的阝，太陽和彈回的光帶在右邊落成昜，拼出橘色的「陽」。
object: a big glossy golden toy sun perched on a small sandy hill, with one long stretchy golden ray-ribbon dangling down
morph: the monster's bottom squashes the hill into the tall left radical 阝; the released sun drops into place as 日 at upper right, and the snapped ray-ribbon springs into the horizontal 一 and the curled, slanted strokes of 勿 beneath it, completing 陽
creativeAngle: 改用拉鋸戰：怪獸與鯊魚各拉太陽光帶的一端，彈開那一瞬間把三個部件（山丘、太陽、光帶）同時甩成阝、日、勿，讓撞擊本身組字；不再是前版的靜態金色雕像慢慢被照亮，也沒有機器人。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip. Teaching subject: the single Traditional Chinese glyph 陽 (sun / sunshine), correctly formed, in solid deep sunset-orange against a pale cream-blue sky, ending centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height with clear margins. Cast: a huge round fuzzy purple cartoon monster with one yellow horn and a goofy grin, and a chunky blue wind-up toy shark with a silver key on its back. Nothing busy behind them.

0.0-1.5s: A small sandy hill sits left of center with a big glossy golden toy sun perched on top; one long stretchy golden ray-ribbon dangles from the sun down to the ground. The fuzzy monster waddles in from the left, eyes going huge at the sun. It turns around to admire it and its bottom bumps the hill, wobbling the sun. As the voice says the first 陽, the monster grabs the ribbon with both paws and the sun glows brighter.

1.5-3.0s: The wind-up shark skitters in from the right, key ticking, and chomps the far end of the ribbon, the wrong thing entirely. Tug-of-war: the monster leans left, the shark leans right, the golden ribbon stretches thin across the whole frame. Feet skid, fur puffs up, both faces turn red, the horn vibrates. One frozen beat of straining.

3.0-4.5s: BOING. The ribbon slips free and both fly backwards onto their bottoms. The monster thumps into the hill, squashing it upward into the tall left radical 阝. The sun pops off and drops into place as 日 at upper right; the snapped ribbon springs across into the horizontal stroke 一 and curls down into the slanted strokes of 勿 below it. The voice says the second 陽 exactly as these pieces snap together into the finished solid orange 陽 at about 70% of frame height. The shark spins in a circle on its belly.

4.5-5.5s: The voice says 太陽 as a soft golden sunrise glow spreads across the sky behind the glyph and the monster, sitting on the left, throws both arms wide in a happy sun shape with a dizzy grin.

5.5-8.0s: The glyph stays perfectly still and readable for the final 3 seconds. Off to the left the monster does a tiny seated wiggle-dance; off to the right the shark slowly winds down with a last tick. Neither touches the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen narrator speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin (Taiwan standard readings, no erhua), reading exactly these syllables with clear tones: 陽、陽、太陽 (ㄧㄤˊ、ㄧㄤˊ、ㄊㄞˋ ㄧㄤˊ). Say the character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. No other speech, subtitles or loud music; the vocabulary word is audio only. The glyph 陽 is the only text on screen: no captions, labels, watermark, logos, clutter, or flashing effects. No real people or realistic human figures; all characters are stylized toys or cartoon creatures.
